transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Yeah, thanks for fitting me in. Um, I guess I'm here because things have just escalated really fast lately. 

I went from barely even settling into my new apartment—which, by the way, has this amazing natural light in the living room, but the property manager is an absolute nightmare about parking. Like, I pay for a spot, but there's always a delivery truck blocking it, and when I tried to call the office they just put me on hold for twenty minutes. But anyway, I went from just trying to unpack my boxes to suddenly saying yes to, well, everything. 

I started doing all these mentoring sessions, I'm taking on extra client prototypes, and I just decided to redesign my entire portfolio from scratch. It was like I had to fix my whole life in one giant design sprint. Speaking of sprints, my old agency used to do these strict two-week Agile sprints and it was just the most exhausting process, especially when the developers wouldn't even read my handoff notes in Figma... but yeah, I just took on way too much all at once and I don't really know why.
How long has this particular burst of extra energy and taking on so many projects been going on—did it start suddenly at a specific point, or has it been more of a lifelong pattern for you?

Well, it's definitely not a lifelong thing, at least not this extreme. This whole intense up-and-down pattern really just started since I moved into the apartment, which was about a month ago. 

And honestly, moving is just the worst, isn't it? I had to hire these movers who completely scratched up my vintage mid-century credenza. I spent months sourcing that piece on Marketplace—it has these beautiful tapered legs and original brass hardware. I even tried buffing out the scratch with this special teak oil I found, but you can still see it if the light hits it a certain way. Which really bothers me because, I don't know, my eye just goes straight to the imperfection. It's like when a call-to-action button on a webpage is off by just two pixels, it just ruins the whole layout for me and I can't look at anything else until I go in and fix the CSS... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what were you asking me? Oh, right, the energy thing. Yeah, just since the move, so about a month.
Before this last month, have you ever gone through a period—lasting two weeks or more—where you felt persistently down, low on energy, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yeah, definitely. Um, those heavier, really low stretches... they actually started showing up around the time of my separation, which was about 11 months ago. Even before this recent move made everything feel so much sharper and more intense, I was having these long periods where I just couldn't get off the couch. 

Which was really hard because my ex and I used to do everything together, especially on weekends. We'd always go to this little farmer's market down the street from our old place. They had this one vendor who sold the most amazing artisan sourdough—like, a perfectly blistered crust, you know? And I tried baking my own sourdough during the pandemic like everyone else, but my starter just completely died after two weeks. I think my apartment was too cold, or maybe I wasn't feeding it right. I read all these blogs about hydration ratios and ambient temperature, and it's actually fascinating how the wild yeast reacts, kind of like how different browsers render web fonts completely differently. Like, Safari is just notorious for messing up kerning... 

But yeah, to answer your question, those really down periods started about 11 months ago, after the separation.
During this past month of increased energy and activity, have you noticed you need much less sleep than usual—like feeling fully rested after only a few hours—without feeling tired the next day?

Yeah, sleep has been... well, non-existent, honestly. For several nights I slept maybe three or four hours, tops, and I'd still wake up completely convinced I was totally fine. I figured I should just use the extra time to get ahead on things. 

Like, I started reorganizing all my design assets at 3 AM. Which, by the way, is a total nightmare because Adobe changed their cloud syncing process again. It used to be so seamless, but now every time I try to access my shared libraries, it throws this weird error code. I ended up spending two hours on a forum reading about how other designers are dealing with it. There was this one guy from Sweden who wrote a custom script to bypass the cloud entirely, which is just brilliant. I tried learning Python a couple of years ago so I could do stuff like that, but I got stuck on the syntax. It's so rigid compared to front-end stuff. I really prefer CSS, you know? It's more visual. 

But yeah, waking up after three hours and feeling totally rested. It's been weird, but I've been getting a lot done.
During this past month, have you felt unusually confident, like you could do anything, or that your abilities or ideas were more special or important than usual?

Um, confident? I don't know if I'd say unusually confident, or like I'm more special than anyone else. I mean, I know I'm good at my job, but I wouldn't say I feel invincible or anything. 

Speaking of my job, though, I did just get this new freelance client who wants a complete overhaul of their e-commerce site. They're selling these artisanal, handcrafted candles, right? And their current site is just a disaster. It looks like it was built in 2005. The typography is all wrong, they're using Comic Sans for the product descriptions—who does that anymore? It's like they don't even care about user experience. I was telling my sister about it, and she just laughed because she knows how much bad fonts bother me. She actually bought me this mug for my birthday that says "I judge you by your font choices." It's hilarious. But also true. Like, if you're trying to sell a forty-dollar candle, you need a sleek, minimalist serif font, maybe some elegant whitespace... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about feeling special or super confident. Yeah, no, I don't think I've really felt like that. Just, you know, focused on getting things done.
During this past month, have you made any impulsive decisions—like spending a lot of money, taking on financial risks, or other actions that were out of character for you?

Yeah, actually, that's... that's been a bit of a problem. I kind of went on a tear with my credit card. I bought all these really expensive light fixtures for my new place, and then I kept buying all these premium design software add-ons because I was convinced I needed them for that candle client. Oh, and I booked a last-minute flight for a trip that I really couldn't afford. 

Which is so frustrating because I'm usually pretty careful with money. My dad was an accountant, so I grew up with him constantly lecturing me about compound interest and the importance of a 401k. He used to make me sit down at the kitchen table every Sunday and balance my checkbook when I was in high school. Which, honestly, who even uses checks anymore? I haven't written a physical check in probably five years. Everything is just Venmo or Apple Pay now. It's so much easier, but it also makes spending money feel less real, you know? Like, you just double-click the side button on your phone and boom, you've spent two hundred dollars. Apple's UI for that is actually incredibly well-designed, the way the little haptic feedback clicks when the payment goes through. It's very satisfying. Maybe a little too satisfying. 

But yeah, I didn't even realize how badly I'd hit my savings until I looked at my statement a few days ago. It was definitely out of character.
